text:
alert-bot: 🚨 [INCIDENT] p99 latency spike on streaming API - observed from 4777769950 to now. Affected pool: shared-gpu-7. p95 -> 420ms (ok), p99 -> 1.2s (baseline ~350ms). Error rate low. Streaming stalls reported. Auto-throttle not triggered. Paging oncall.

jamie: acked pager. i'm on my way, will join. which tenants are hot? :eyes:

ana (ana): im oncall. looking at metrics now — io wait on nodes backing shared-gpu-7 is high (nvme avg qdepth ~190). top noisy tenant looks like tenant-889 (bursting large batch tensor downloads).

kai: adding context: cgroup blkio writeback is spiking on those hosts, kernel logs show repeated writeback_cgroup warnings. suspect noisy download + checkpoint writes from tenant-889.

monica: FYI cs reported degraded streaming for customer: mediaflow (customer id mf-22) — live transcription sessions are stuttering. customer impact: mid-priority but multiple active sessions.

jamie: ok mitigation plan: 1) throttle tenant-889 cgroup to 30-50% IO, 2) evict if still noisy, 3) temporarily shift mf-22 traffic to reserved-dedicated-3 pool (low-latency). Can someone run the throttle?

eng-runtime: i can apply an IO throttle via rictl on the host group. preparing command now.

eng-runtime: running:
```
rictl cgroup throttle --tenant tenant-889 --device /dev/nvme0n1 --rwmbps 200MB
```
output: queued on hosts: host-37a, host-37b, host-38c.

alert-bot: pagerduty: incident acknowledged by ana at 4777770012.

ana: throttle applied to tenant-889 on host-37a/37b/38c. monitoring p99.

kai: also adding temporary KV cache eviction to free RAM and reduce NVMe writebacks:
```
rictl kvcache evict --pool shared-gpu-7 --percent 50
```

jamie: good. watch metrics + streaming traces. if p99 comes down, keep for 10m then gradually relax. if not, plan B: evict the tenant.

monica: moving mf-22 to reserved pool now via traffic-router. command:
```
trafficctl route --from pool=shared-gpu-7 --to pool=reserved-dedicated-3 --tenant mf-22 --immediate
```
status: in progress on 3 sessions.

eng-runtime: after throttle, p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 480ms within 40s. streaming stall counts down 70%. :thumbsup:

ana: customer cs notified: "we're seeing improved latency and actively routing your sessions to a dedicated pool, monitoring continues."

jamie: great. hold throttle for 15m monitoring window. nominate eng-runtime to own follow-up (perf patch), kai to own kernel logs/cgroup tuning, ana to monitor oncall for the remainder of shift. I'll create a postmortem ticket and include checklist for automatic eviction thresholds.

eng-runtime: taking follow-up. will capture perf traces and open a PR with a safer default writeback qdepth for shared pools.

kai: grabbing dmesg and iostat logs now, copying to /incident/4777770000/logs. snippet:
```
[ 12345.678901] writeback_cgroup: throttle: cgroup writeback exceeded 1000ms
[ 12345.679012] nvme nvme0: I/O 94 backlog: 190
```

jamie: handoff: ana you're primary for the remainder of the oncall window — escalate to infra lead if noisy tenant reappears or if auto-throttle fails to engage. tagging @deploy-bot to schedule a canary configuration to avoid regression.

deploy-bot: noted. scheduling config canary: patch id cfg-889-io-qos to 10% of hosts in prod at 4777770400.

ana: confirmed last check p99 420-520ms, stall events minimal. keeping monitor.

monica: CS updated and customer alerted to improvement. ticket updated with mitigation steps.

jamie: closing live page for now, leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :shipit: 

eng-runtime: will attach perf tarball and suggested quantized checkpoint flow to the ticket.

alert-bot: incident auto-close condition: p99 < 600ms for 10m and stall count <= baseline. monitoring continues.
